question: In a patient with a confirmed phaeochromocytoma, a beta-blocker should be given first to control the tachycardia before an alpha-blocker is added to control hypertension.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Always establish alpha-blockade (e.g., phenoxybenzamine) first to prevent unopposed vasoconstriction; a beta-blocker is added only afterwards to manage reflex tachycardia.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Beta-blockade before alpha-blockade is dangerous: blocking the beta-2 vasodilatory effect while catecholamine excess persists causes unopposed alpha-mediated vasoconstriction, producing a hypertensive crisis.
